instruction:
Fix `packages/element/src/textStyles.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major (line 592): RE_LTR_STRONG_OR_DIGIT classifies European digits 0-9 as strong "L" instead of weak European Numbers ("EN"). On an LTR-base line (baseDirection === "ltr") containing an RTL span with European digits (e.g. "Item: مرحبا 123 عالم"), resolveLineCharDirections and getLineTextRuns assign "123" and its adjacent spaces direction "ltr" at level 0 instead of resolving the spaces to "rtl" (level 1, per UAX#9 W2/N1) and the digits to level 2 (per UAX#9 I1/I2), splitting the RTL run in two so "مرحبا" and "عالم" fail to reverse visually around "123". — fix: Treat ASCII digits [0-9] as weak "EN" in resolveLineCharDirections/getLineTextRuns: when the preceding strong character is "R", treat "EN" as "R" for adjacent neutral resolution (so spaces between "R" and "EN" get level 1 "rtl") while assigning the "EN" run direction "ltr" at embedding level 2, and split logical runs when either direction or level changes.
